content:
violet_sales: Urgent POC blocker with ClearLedger. They say their app resolves our private hostname but calls either time out or return 403. Demo in ~30h, can we swarm?
omar_se: Do we have the resolved IP and whether they peered VPCs or set up an interface endpoint in their VPC?
yasmin_netops: Customer told us they set up a VPC peering between their app VPC (vpc-a) and an infra VPC (vpc-b) owned by their infra team where they believed the VPCE existed. They see DNS resolve to 10.100.50.7 and can ping that IP from their app VPC. Trouble is interface VPCEs are not reachable over VPC peering by default. Does that match?
violet_sales: That sounds plausible. They assumed peering would route to the endpoint. Their ops sent this curl:
```
curl -v https://internal-api.redwood/ping --resolve internal-api.redwood:443:10.100.50.7 -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden {"error":"AccessDenied","message":"principal not authorized"}`
omar_se: Two separate issues could be conflated: 1) DNS resolution might be returning an IP in the infra VPC (10.100.50.7) which is reachable via peering, but that IP is an ENI for a VPCE that only accepts traffic from the same VPC or from approved source VPCs via PrivateLink. 2) If traffic is hairpinned into a different service in vpc-b, the auth principal might not map and we get 403.
harry_sre: Quick network checks ask them to run from an instance in app VPC: `nc -vz 10.100.50.7 443` and `traceroute -n 10.100.50.7` and paste outputs. If TCP connects but TLS shows our cert only when endpoint is in the same VPC, then peering is the issue.
yasmin_netops: Important AWS note: Interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) are regional and tied to the ENIs managed in the account where the endpoint was created. Traffic to an interface endpoint's ENI won't be routed over VPC peering to the service in another account. To access a service via PrivateLink across accounts you need the service owner to expose an endpoint service and the consumer to create a local interface endpoint in their VPC that connects to the service.
mira_security: Also request the JWT claims (sanitized `iss` and `org_id`). If they incorrectly terminate TLS in the infra VPC or a proxy there, Authorization could be lost. But first fix the routing.
infra-bot: started: vpce:validate-access --vpce-ip 10.100.50.7 --from-vpc vpc-aaaa1111
omar_se: If they cannot create an interface endpoint in their app VPC, options: 1) Have infra create an endpoint service (PrivateLink) and grant permission so their app VPC can create a local VPCE that connects across accounts. 2) Use Transit Gateway with endpoint routing (more complex) or 3) provide a short-lived public staging endpoint for demo.
yasmin_netops: Example command for them to verify VPCE presence: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=addresses.private-ip-address,Values=10.100.50.7 --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].Description'` and `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=dns-entry.Value,Values=internal-api.redwood*` to see which VPC owns the endpoint.
harry_sre: If they insist traffic is reaching our side but getting 403, ask them to paste the sanitized VPCE policy JSON and the IAM principal ARN their app actually uses at runtime. Many teams create a policy that allows only specific source VPC IDs or VPCE IDs which blocks cross-account access.
violet_sales: They're asking about quick workarounds because their infra team won't create an endpoint until security signs off. Any short-term solution?
omar_se: Fastest for a demo: 1) create a temporary public staging hostname (HTTPS) that bypasses Private DNS and VPC restrictions, or 2) spin up a tiny bastion in the app VPC and curl via `--resolve` to the VPCE IP to demonstrate functionality. If security requires PrivateLink we can offer to help them set up the endpoint connection.
mira_security: If we go with temporary public endpoint, we'll need to document data handling and ensure tokens/org validation remains identical. Offer mutual TLS only if they insist on cert-level assurances but note that onboarding client certs takes days.
yasmin_netops: I'll draft an ops checklist to send their infra: (1) confirm where 10.100.50.7 is owned (describe-network-interfaces), (2) if it's our account, please create an interface endpoint in your app VPC that connects to our endpoint service, (3) share sanitized VPCE policy for review, (4) verify there are no restrictive `aws:SourceVpc` conditions.
infra-bot: vpce:validate-access results: endpoint not reachable via peering - recommendation: create local interface endpoint or use endpoint service
harry_sre: TL;DR: VPC peering will not proxy to another account's interface endpoint. Create a consumer interface endpoint (PrivateLink) in the app VPC or use our endpoint service. Once they create a local VPCE, if they still get 403 we'll check token claims and endpoint policy.
violet_sales: Great. I'll send the checklist and offer the staging-hostname/demo-host option. Also asking sales ops for a 2-week POC pricing for a private link setup we can help them configure. Thanks team!
